record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: uniqueness of the radial Ginzburg-Landau solution
record.original_question: Let Omega be the unit disc in R^2, let epsilon > 0, and consider maps u: Omega -> R^2 solving the Ginzburg-Landau system Delta u = epsilon^{-2} u(1 - |u|^2) in Omega with boundary value u(x)=x on the boundary. The source defines the radial solution U_epsilon(x) = (x/|x|) f_epsilon(|x|), where f_epsilon solves the associated radial ODE with f_epsilon(0)=0 and f_epsilon(1)=1. Is this radial solution U_epsilon the only solution of the Ginzburg-Landau boundary value problem?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.1 ([3, Problem 10 in Chapter XI]). Is the radial solution U_epsilon the only solution of (2.1)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : |x| < 1\}$ be the open unit disc in $\mathbb{R}^2$, and let $\varepsilon > 0$. Consider maps $u : \overline{\Omega} \to \mathbb{R}^2$ satisfying the Ginzburg–Landau boundary value problem
$$\Delta u = \frac{1}{\varepsilon^2}\, u\bigl(|u|^2 - 1\bigr) \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u(x) = x \quad \text{for } |x| = 1.$$
Define the radial solution $U_\varepsilon : \overline{\Omega} \to \mathbb{R}^2$ by
$$U_\varepsilon(x) = \frac{x}{|x|}\, f_\varepsilon(|x|),$$
where $f_\varepsilon : [0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$ is the unique solution of the ordinary differential equation
$$f_\varepsilon''(r) + \frac{1}{r} f_\varepsilon'(r) - \frac{1}{r^2} f_\varepsilon(r) = \frac{1}{\varepsilon^2} f_\varepsilon(r)\bigl(f_\varepsilon(r)^2 - 1\bigr), \quad r \in (0,1),$$
with $f_\varepsilon(0) = 0$ and $f_\varepsilon(1) = 1$.

Is $U_\varepsilon$ the only solution of the above boundary value problem?
artifact.status_search_result: Uniqueness of the radial solution to this Dirichlet problem on the disc is a long-standing question of Brezis. Partial results are known: Mironescu proved that for small $\varepsilon$ the radial solution is the unique minimizer (and radially symmetric), and Ignat–Nguyen–Slastikov–Zarnescu established uniqueness of minimizers when either the energy or the Ginzburg–Landau parameter is small. Uniqueness among all critical points (the full open problem) does not appear to be resolved in the literature.

status_evidence.title: On the uniqueness of minimisers of Ginzburg-Landau functionals
status_evidence.snippet: Ginzburg-Landau minimizers with zero degree Dirichlet boundary condition are shown to be unique whenever either the energy or the Ginzburg-Landau parameter are small.
status_evidence.claim: Uniqueness of minimizers established in restricted regimes, suggesting full uniqueness among critical points remains open.

status_evidence.title: Les minimiseurs locaux pour l'équation de Ginzburg-Landau (Mironescu)
status_evidence.snippet: Mironescu proved that local minimizers for the Ginzburg-Landau equation have radial symmetry.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: local minimizers are radially symmetric, but this does not settle uniqueness among all solutions.
